Physical problem

Sunday morning in a shared kitchen: you have made filter coffee and filled two identical cups with 200 ml each. Then the phone rings, and the call will last an hour. Your flatmate pours his milk into the coffee straight away (cup 1). You put your cup next to it and want to add the milk only after the call (cup 2), so that the coffee “stays hot for longer”. In both cases the milk comes straight from the fridge.

Your flatmate says: “It doesn’t matter whether you add the milk straight away or later. Energy is conserved, after all.” Which cup is warmer after an hour?

Both cups release heat to the room through their surface, and the warmer the contents are compared with the room, the more heat they release. The simulation calculates the process with the transient lumped energy balance from Tutorial 5; when going further, you can change amounts, temperatures, cup and mug.
